trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide:
The platinum is the prize for everything else — it pops the moment the other 54 trophies are yours, so treat it as a checklist, not a task of its own.
Work through the seven roadmap stages in order: story first, strands before the finale, then the activity, collectible and money sweeps.
Save the missable strand finales and the choice-based trophy for before the final mission, so nothing is locked out.
Finish at 100% completion and the platinum lands with the last trophy you earn.
sources: PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap
PlayStation official trophy list

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide:
This is the opening mission, so it comes to you — just play the story from the start and it pops when the mission ends.
Follow the opening beats: meet the characters, drive where the marker tells you, and finish the fishing scene that gives the mission its name.
There is no way to miss it and no preparation needed; it is the first trophy most players earn.
If you are replaying, it unlocks again on any fresh story run.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list
PlayStation official trophy list

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide:
Chapter 1 is the first act of the story, so this trophy is simply a matter of playing through its missions in order.
Work the mission markers as they appear; each completed mission moves the chapter forward and the trophy pops at the chapter's final cutscene.
There is nothing optional to chase here — side content can wait until later roadmap stages.
Keep a backup save before the chapter's big story choice, since a later trophy depends on choices you make.
sources: PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide
PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide:
Chapter 2 continues directly from the first, so keep following the story markers in order.
The chapter builds the crew and the money troubles that drive the rest of the game; finish its missions one by one and the trophy pops at the final scene.
No side activity is required — the chapter's own missions are all that count.
Between missions, use the downtime to try a shooting range or a race, since those feed later activity trophies.
sources: PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap
Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide:
Chapter 3 opens up Vice City proper, so expect more driving, more choices and bigger set pieces.
Play the missions in the order the game offers them; the trophy pops when the chapter's last mission ends.
This is a good chapter to start noticing stranger markers on the map — the strands they open matter for missable trophies later.
Do not start the final mission until every stranger strand is finished, a rule that matters from here on.
sources: PlayStation official trophy list
PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide:
Chapter 4 is the last full chapter before the endgame, and its missions are the longest in the game.
Push through the story markers in order; the trophy pops at the chapter's closing scene.
Before the chapter ends, check your stranger strands — any finale not yet done should be finished now, while the world is still open.
Keep a manual save here too: the endgame choices are close, and one trophy depends on them.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list
PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide:
This gold trophy is the story's ending — finish the final mission and it is yours.
Before you start it, do the missable check: all seven stranger strand finales done, all 8 strands complete, and a backup save made before the story choices.
The final mission itself is long and checkpointed, so play it straight through and let the story carry you.
Once it pops, the world opens up for the cleanup stages: activities, collectibles and money.
sources: PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide
PlayStation official trophy list

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide:
Breakfast Run is a story mission in the early chapters — follow the story markers until it appears, then play it through.
The mission is a run with a partner, so keep pace with the route markers and do not stray from the plan the game lays out.
It is unmissable as long as you keep playing the story, and it pops at the mission's end.
Note the partner mechanics it teaches: they come back for the partner trophies in the later stages.
sources: PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap
Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide:
The Cartel Heist is a story heist mission — it appears on the story path, so keep playing the chapters until the marker shows up.
Prepare before it starts: stock up on ammo and armour, since heists do not pause for shopping.
Follow the crew's plan through the setup and the getaway; the trophy pops when the heist is done.
The heist also teaches the robbery flow you will reuse for the bank-vault and armored-truck trophies later.
sources: PlayStation official trophy list
PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide:
Child's Play is a story mission on the main path — play the chapters until its marker appears.
The mission leans on family ties in the story, so expect a character-driven sequence rather than a straight shootout.
Complete it and the trophy pops at the end; nothing outside the mission is required.
If you are tracking the story trophies in order, this is one of the mid-chapter beats worth ticking off as you go.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list
PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide:
Headliners is a story mission — keep following the chapter markers until it unlocks.
The mission is a headline set piece, so expect a big scene with plenty of action; stock up beforehand and follow the on-screen objectives.
Finish it and the trophy pops; there is no missable element to it.
It is a good moment to check your strand progress, since the mid-game is when stranger markers start appearing in numbers.
sources: PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide
Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide:
VCIA Takedown is a story mission at the airport — play the story until the marker appears.
The mission takes place around Vice City International Airport, so expect tight corridors and vehicle sections.
Complete the takedown as directed and the trophy pops at the mission's end.
The airport area you learn here is the same one the unscheduled-departure trophy uses later, so remember the layout.
sources: PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap
PlayStation official trophy list

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide:
Operation Savage Glory is a late-story mission — keep playing the chapters until it appears.
It is one of the biggest operations in the game, so go in with full ammo, armour and a plan for the firefights.
Finish the operation and the trophy pops; it is the last named mission trophy before the final mission itself.
After this, do your final missable check before starting the finale.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list
PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide:
100% completion is the long tail of the platinum: every story mission, strand, activity, collectible and side task the game counts.
Work the roadmap in order and use the in-game completion checklist to see what is left — it tracks missions, strands, activities, collectibles and the money goals.
The last few percent are usually a missed collectible or an unfinished activity, so sweep those systematically by district.
When the counter hits 100%, this gold trophy pops and the platinum is one step away.
sources: PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap
PlayStation official trophy list

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide:
Stunts are the jumps, near-misses, airtime and drifts the game counts as you drive hard — 250 of them, tracked on the counter.
The fastest way is to chain them: find a stretch with ramps and traffic, then jump, drift and near-miss in the same run so each move banks a stunt.
Use fast bikes and cars with good air control, and replay stunt-friendly spots rather than hunting for new ones.
Log your count with the stepper here and keep at it in short bursts between other goals — it adds up faster than it looks.
sources: PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide
Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide:
Leonida is packed with activities, and this trophy asks you to sample each type once — no wins or medals needed, just a try.
Work through the list: a race, a shooting-range challenge, a drone race, fishing, an arcade game, meditation, hunting, a challenge and the rest of the activity menu.
Open the activities menu or the map filters to see which types you have not touched yet.
Do this early in the activities sweep — it also unlocks the venues you will revisit for the deeper activity trophies.
sources: PlayStation official trophy list
PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide:
The Shooting Range holds 42 challenges, and every one of them needs a gold medal — this is the toughest pure-skill trophy in the set.
Start with the weapon types you are best at and learn each challenge's target pattern before chasing the gold time.
Use the range's practice runs to memorise spawn points, then go for gold when the pattern is second nature.
Work through the challenges a few at a time between other goals; 42 golds is a marathon, not a sprint.
sources: PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap
PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide:
Top Fun runs drone races at several locations across Leonida, and you need a win at every one of them.
Visit each location in turn and race the course until you win — learn the gates and the tight corners on a practice run first.
Drones handle differently from cars, so brake early into turns and cut the racing line through the gates.
The map marks the locations, so tick them off one by one and the trophy pops after the last win.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list
PlayStation official trophy list

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide:
Twenty different races, twenty wins — each race on the map counts once, so variety matters more than repetition.
Pick the shortest circuits first and learn the field: the AI is beatable with a clean racing line and a fast car in the right class.
Work through the map region by region, ticking each race off as you win it.
Replays of a race you already won do not add to the count, so keep moving to new races until the 20th win pops the trophy.
sources: PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide
PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide:
Cal is the fishing rival — challenge him at a fishing spot and beat his catch.
Pick a spot with good fish, cast where the water ripples, and work the line patiently: reel in when the fish runs, ease off when it fights.
If Cal wins the first round, challenge him again — the trophy is about beating him once, not about a perfect streak.
Fishing also feeds the story's opening mission, so the mechanics will feel familiar by the time you face him.
sources: PlayStation official trophy list
Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide:
Walk into any arcade in Leonida, pick a cabinet and finish one full game — any title counts.
Arcade games are short, so try the simplest cabinet first and learn its controls in the opening seconds.
You do not need a high score, just a completed game, and the trophy pops when it ends.
Arcades are also a good way to pass in-game time between story beats.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list
PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide:
Andy is one of the strangers with a mission strand — a chain of missions that ends in a finale, and this trophy is that finale.
Pick up Andy's strand from its map marker and play each mission in the chain as it appears; the strand only advances when you finish the current mission.
Reach the final mission for Andy and complete it to pop the trophy.
Do it before the final story mission: strand finales are missable once the story ends.
sources: PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap
PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide
trophies.missableNote: Missable: Andy's strand finale must be completed before you start the final story mission. Finish all stranger strands first.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide:
Kenton's strand is a chain of stranger missions that ends in a finale on the water — this trophy is that last mission.
Find Kenton's marker, work through the strand's missions in order, and keep an eye on the map: new missions appear only after the previous one is done.
Complete the final mission for Kenton and the trophy pops.
Like every strand finale, it must be finished before the final story mission, so do not leave it until the endgame.
sources: PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide
PlayStation official trophy list
trophies.missableNote: Missable: Kenton's strand finale must be completed before you start the final story mission. Finish all stranger strands first.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide:
Billy's strand is a lone-rider chain of stranger missions — follow the marker, finish each mission, and the next one unlocks.
The strand builds to a final mission for Billy; complete it and the trophy pops.
Billy's missions lean on riding, so bring a fast bike and expect open-road chases.
Finish it before the final story mission: strand finales cannot be completed after the story ends.
sources: PlayStation official trophy list
Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list
trophies.missableNote: Missable: Billy's strand finale must be completed before you start the final story mission. Finish all stranger strands first.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide:
Eight stranger strands, eight complete chains — this silver trophy tracks the lot, and it is missable because the strands close at the endgame.
Work the stranger markers across the map: Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone and the other strands each count as one when their chain is finished.
Do not rush the story: explore between chapters so new stranger markers have time to appear.
Finish the eighth strand before the final mission and the trophy pops with it.
sources: PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap
Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list
trophies.missableNote: Missable: all 8 stranger strands must be completed before you start the final story mission. Do them during the story, not after.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide:
Randy's strand is a supply-chain chain of stranger missions — pick it up from its marker and work through it mission by mission.
The chain ends in a final mission for Randy; complete it and the trophy pops.
Expect deliveries, deals and a shootout or two along the way, so stock up between missions.
Finish Randy's finale before the final story mission, as with every strand finale.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list
PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide
trophies.missableNote: Missable: Randy's strand finale must be completed before you start the final story mission. Finish all stranger strands first.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide:
Tyrone's strand is the last of the named stranger chains — find his marker and play the missions in order.
The strand ends in a final mission for Tyrone; finish it and the trophy pops.
Tyrone's missions are punchy and fast, so keep a good car nearby and expect the chain to move quickly once started.
Complete it before the final story mission — after the ending, the strand is gone for this playthrough.
sources: PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide
PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap
trophies.missableNote: Missable: Tyrone's strand finale must be completed before you start the final story mission. Finish all stranger strands first.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide:
Meditation spots are scattered across Leonida — quiet places where you can sit and meditate, and you need to visit every one.
Open the map and look for the meditation markers; visit them district by district so none is missed.
At each spot, start the meditation and let the sequence play out to count it.
Pair this with the exploration trophy: meditating at a new spot also helps you discover the area around it.
sources: PlayStation official trophy list
PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide:
Bret wants a unique animal hunted — a one-of-a-kind creature, not a common deer.
Talk to Bret to get the hunt started, then follow the trail markers to the animal's territory.
Track it quietly, take the shot when it is clean, and bring the proof back to Bret.
The hunt is a single set piece, so it is over quickly once you know where the animal roams.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list
PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide:
Collectible cards are hidden around Leonida in sets, and you need three complete sets.
Cards turn up in shops, interiors and out-of-the-way spots — check the map's collectible hints and sweep each district methodically.
A set is complete when every card in it is found, so keep a list of which sets are close to done and finish those first.
Three finished sets pop the trophy; the remaining sets are still worth grabbing for 100% completion.
sources: PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide
PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide:
WAiNK It is the game's photo-sharing gag: snap the WAiNK pose at 100 different locations across Leonida.
The counter tracks distinct spots, so variety is everything — a new district, a landmark, a beach, a rooftop all count once each.
Work through the map region by region, hitting the obvious landmarks first and the quiet corners after.
Use the counter stepper here to log your progress; 100 spots is a long sweep, best done a district at a time.
sources: PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap
PlayStation official trophy list

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide:
Challenges are the game's small goals — stunt chains, driving feats, combat tasks and more — and you need 50 of them done.
Open the challenges menu to see what is available; pick the easy ones first (short stunts, simple driving goals) and bank them fast.
Many challenges complete naturally while you chase other trophies, so check the menu regularly and mop up the stragglers.
Fifty done pops the trophy; the counter stepper here helps you track the total.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list
PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide:
This is a partner trophy: get a 4-star wanted level with your partner beside you, then lose the cops together.
Start trouble somewhere open — the docks or the highways — until the fourth star appears, then break line of sight and hide.
Use alleys, tunnels and the partner's driving to shake the search cone; the wanted level drops when the cops lose you.
Escape with your partner still with you and the trophy pops — if your partner is left behind, try again.
sources: PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide
PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide:
Rob three shops in a row with your partner — and keep your wanted level the whole time, so speed and planning matter.
Pick three shops close together on the map, plan the route, and hit them one after another without stopping.
Keep the getaways clean: no cops spotting you between robberies, or the chain breaks and you start over.
Three robberies in a row with the wanted level intact pops the trophy.
sources: PlayStation official trophy list
Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide:
One hundred different vehicles to discover — drive it, and it counts.
Variety is the whole game: cars, bikes, trucks, boats and aircraft all add to the total, and rare spawns count the same as common ones.
Sweep new districts and check parking lots, docks and airfields for models you have not driven yet.
The counter stepper here tracks your total; keep hopping into anything unfamiliar and the trophy pops at 100.
sources: PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap
PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide:
Combat Focus slows time and lets you pick targets — take down five enemies in one activation.
Find a spot with a cluster of enemies, like a gang hideout or a shootout, and wait until five are in view.
Trigger Combat Focus, snap between targets quickly, and make every shot count before the meter runs out.
If you only get four, reload the checkpoint and try again — the setup matters more than the aim.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list
PlayStation official trophy list

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide:
VCIA is Vice City International Airport, and an unscheduled departure means leaving by air without a ticket — steal a plane and take off.
Get airside, find a plane on the tarmac, and get it moving before security closes in.
Once you are airborne and clear of the airport, the trophy pops.
Go in with a fast vehicle for the approach and expect a wanted level on the way out.
sources: PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide
PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide:
Rhinos are the tanks of Leonida, and this trophy is about getting into one — or dealing with one up close.
Find a Rhino at a military area or during a high-wanted-level response, then get inside it and drive.
Tanks are slow but unstoppable, so once you are in, the trophy is yours for the taking.
Expect heavy police attention while you are in it, so enjoy the ride and get out before it is destroyed.
sources: PlayStation official trophy list
Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide:
A clean jewelry-store robbery: get in, take the goods and get out without anyone raising the alarm.
Scout the store first — learn the guard patrols and the camera angles, then move when the floor is clear.
Go quiet: no gunfire, no alarms, no witnesses calling it in.
Slip out the way you came and the trophy pops once you are clear; if you are spotted, restart the attempt.
sources: PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap
PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide:
Five bank vaults, five clean escapes — the biggest robbery trophy in the game.
Plan each vault like a heist: scout the bank, hit it fast, and have a getaway car parked close by.
Escape means breaking the wanted level after the robbery, so use tunnels, alleys and fast cars to vanish.
Five vaults robbed and escaped pops the trophy; do them one at a time between other goals so the wanted levels stay manageable.
sources: PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide
Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide:
Armored trucks cruise the highways of Leonida — stop one, crack it open and escape with the cash.
Spot a truck on the road, block it or ram it to a stop, then deal with the guards and the lock.
Grab the money fast and break away before the police response builds.
Escape the wanted level and the trophy pops — a classic blitz, done in minutes once you know the truck routes.
sources: PlayStation official trophy list
PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide:
Explore every corner of Leonida — the map fills in as you travel, and this trophy pops when the whole state is covered.
Drive the highways, the back roads and the coast; the game counts districts and regions as you enter them.
Use the map's fog as your guide: any greyed-out area is somewhere you have not been yet.
Pair this with the collectible and WAiNK sweeps so every trip does double duty.
sources: PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap
PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide:
Every gang in Leonida runs illegal operations, and you need to rob one from each of them.
Find the gang operations on the map — they are marked once you learn the territories — and hit one per gang.
Each robbery is a short smash-and-grab: get in, take the goods, get out before the gang and the cops converge.
Rob the last gang's operation and the trophy pops.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list
PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide:
Ocean Beach is the postcard end of Vice City — find a beachfront bar, order a cocktail and enjoy the view.
Walk the Ocean Drive strip until you find a bar with a terrace, then sit down and order.
The trophy is a quiet moment, not a challenge: one drink, one view, and it pops.
It is a good palate cleanser between the big robbery and strand stages.
sources: PlayStation official trophy list
PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide:
Find a vehicle showroom, get inside in a car, and smash your way out through the glass — classic style.
Drive in through the front, pick up speed inside, and burst out through the showroom window.
The trophy pops on the exit, so make the smash count the first time.
Expect a wanted level and a repair bill, but the moment is worth it.
sources: PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide
Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide:
Kolt & Associates run a bowling alley in Leonida — walk in, rent a lane and bowl a game.
The alley is on the map once you are near it; go inside, pick up a ball and play through a full game.
You do not need a strike or a high score — just follow through and finish the game.
The trophy pops at the end of the game, and the alley stays open for rematches.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list
PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide:
This is a partnership moment — a scene with your in-game partner that lands with the public.
It unlocks through the story's partner beats, so keep playing the partner missions as they appear.
When the moment arrives, play it through and the trophy pops.
If you are unsure where you are, check the partner missions on the map — the trophy follows from them, not from freeroam.
sources: PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap
PlayStation official trophy list

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide:
Some story choices change what happens next, and this trophy tracks the choices you make — for better or worse.
The key is a backup save: before every big story choice, save manually in a separate slot so you can see the other outcome.
Make the choices as the story offers them; the trophy pops once the tracked choices are made.
If a choice locks you out of something else, reload the backup save and take the other path — that is what the save is for.
sources: PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide
PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap
trophies.missableNote: Missable: choice-based. Keep a manual backup save before every big story choice — once a choice is locked in, you cannot undo it on that playthrough.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide:
Second time's the charm: fail something, then succeed on the very next try.
The simplest route is a mission or activity you can retry — fail it once, then pass it immediately after.
Do not reload a save between the attempts; the trophy tracks the fail-then-pass sequence as it happens.
When the second attempt succeeds, the trophy pops.
sources: PlayStation official trophy list
Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide:
Something strange happens in Leonida — a weird event, a mystery, a moment that makes you ask what just happened.
The trigger is a specific place and time: explore the odd corners of the map, the places that feel out of place, and stay alert for strange happenings.
When the event fires, let it play out to the end and the trophy pops.
If you miss it the first time, revisit the spot — strange events in Leonida tend to repeat.
sources: PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap
PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide:
A melee drive-by with a bowling flavour: knock someone over from a moving vehicle with a melee weapon.
Get a car, pick up a melee weapon, and drive past a target at speed — swing as you pass.
The bowling connection is the alley: practice the timing near Kolt & Associates, where pedestrians are plentiful.
Land the hit from the moving vehicle and the trophy pops.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list
PlayStation official trophy list

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide:
Marked bills are dirty money, and your contacts launder them for a cut — you need $250,000 cleaned in total.
Earn marked bills from robberies and gang operations, then hand them to your laundering contacts through the phone or the map markers.
Each laundered batch adds to the total, so keep the cycle going: rob, launder, repeat.
The bank-vault and gang-operation trophies feed this one directly, so do them together and the $250,000 arrives sooner.
sources: PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide
PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide:
Spend $100,000 across the shops of Leonida — clothes, weapons, cars, property, it all counts.
The easiest path is the expensive one: buy a high-end car or a weapon loadout and the total jumps fast.
Every shop purchase adds up, so just keep buying what you need as you play and check the total now and then.
Save this for after the money goals are done, when your wallet is fullest.
sources: PlayStation official trophy list
Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide:
Garage properties are for sale across Leonida, and you need to own every one of them.
Check the property markers on the map and buy each garage as you can afford it — they are also useful for storing your best cars.
The total cost is steep, so do this after the money-making stages when your funds are high.
Buy the last garage and the trophy pops.
sources: PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Roadmap
PowerPyx — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide:
The Scooter Bros app lets you register vehicles — ten of them, and the trophy is yours.
Open the app on your phone, pick a vehicle you own or have found, and register it to the app.
Any ten vehicles count, so register the ones you drive most and top up with anything new you discover.
Ten registrations pop the trophy; it pairs neatly with the 100-vehicle discovery sweep.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI Achievements / Trophies list
